text_blocks.snippet: Dengue fever symptoms typically appear 4 to 10 days after a bite from an infected mosquito, marked by a sudden high fever (up to 104°F / 40°C) and intense body aches known as "breakbone fever".
snippet_highlighted_words: sudden high fever (up to 104°F / 40°C) and intense body aches known as "breakbone fever"

list.snippet: High Fever: Sudden onset of fever lasting 2 to 7 days.
Severe Headaches: Intense pain, often located behind the eyes (retro-orbital pain) that worsens with eye movement.
Body Aches: Severe muscle, bone, and joint pain.
Skin Rash: A flat or slightly raised red rash that may appear around day 3 or 4, often starting on the chest and spreading.
Gastrointestinal Issues: Nausea, vomiting, and loss of appetite.

text_blocks.snippet: Warning signs usually emerge 24 to 48 hours after the fever subsides (often around days 3 to 7). Severe dengue is a medical emergency. Watch for:

list.snippet: Persistent or repeated vomiting (3 or more times in 24 hours, or vomiting blood)
Bleeding from the nose, gums, or skin (bruising), or blood in the stool or urine
Signs of shock (cold, clammy skin and a rapid, weak pulse)

text_blocks.snippet: Official guidance and symptom criteria can be reviewed via the National Center for Vector Borne Diseases Control or the Mayo Clinic.
